cambrian.name: Cambrian
cambrian.blurb: Most major animal groups appear in the fossil record, including the first trilobites.

ordovician.name: Ordovician
ordovician.blurb: Seas fill with trilobites, brachiopods, and early reef builders, and the period ends in a major mass extinction.

silurian.name: Silurian
silurian.blurb: Coral reefs spread through warm shallow seas while the first vascular plants take hold on land.

devonian.name: Devonian
devonian.blurb: The Age of Fishes, when the first forests grow and the first four-limbed animals appear.

carboniferous.name: Carboniferous
carboniferous.blurb: Swamp forests of giant lycopsids like Lepidodendron lay down coal, and the first reptiles appear.

permian.name: Permian
permian.blurb: Glossopteris forests cover Gondwana, and the period ends in the largest mass extinction in Earth's history.

triassic.name: Triassic
triassic.blurb: Life recovers from the Permian extinction, and the first dinosaurs and mammals appear.

jurassic.name: Jurassic
jurassic.blurb: Giant sauropods walk the land while ammonites and belemnites fill the seas.

cretaceous.name: Cretaceous
cretaceous.blurb: Flowering plants spread, and dinosaurs like Triceratops and Tyrannosaurus live until the asteroid impact 66 million years ago.

paleogene.name: Paleogene
paleogene.blurb: Mammals diversify after the dinosaurs disappear, and the first whales and primates appear.

neogene.name: Neogene
neogene.blurb: Grasslands spread, giant sharks like Otodus hunt the oceans, and early human relatives appear.

quaternary.name: Quaternary
quaternary.blurb: Ice ages come and go, mammoths roam, and modern humans spread across the globe.
